item.title: Minnesota: Helicopter crashes near Airlake Airport, bursts into flames, leaving no survivors; FAA and NTSB launch probe
item.description: A Robinson R66 helicopter crashed and caught fire near Airlake Airport in Minnesota on Saturday afternoon, resulting in no survivors. The crash occurred in a non-residential area, with the NTSB and FAA launching an investigation into the cause. The helicopter, which can seat up to five people, was found west of the airport.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What happened during US raid on Hyundai's plant? Workers hid in air ducts, plunged into pond; 475 Koreans arrested - inside the chaos
item.description: A massive immigration raid at a Hyundai plant in Georgia led to the arrest of 475 workers, predominantly Korean nationals, triggering diplomatic intervention from South Korea. Federal agents executed the operation following a months-long investigation into unlawful employment practices. The raid involved multiple agencies, highlighting a crackdown on workforce exploitation and federal law violations, as stated by Homeland Security.

item.title: Floyd Mayweather net worth in 2025: Inside his boxing, endorsements, and business ventures
item.description: Floyd Mayweather Jr., known as "Money," has amassed a $500 million fortune by 2025, solidifying his status as boxing's wealthiest figure. His earnings stem from record-breaking fights against Conor McGregor and Manny Pacquiao, complemented by strategic investments in real estate, including New York City apartments.

item.title: 'False villainization': Hindu American Foundation director speaks up on Peter Navarro's 'Brahmin' attack
item.description: Peter Navarro's remark about "Brahmins" profiting from India's oil trade with Russia has sparked controversy. Hindu organizations have condemned the statement as a slur and Hinduphobic, drawing comparisons to anti-Semitic tropes. The comment has ignited debate over whether Navarro was referring to the Indian caste or wealthy elites, leading to calls for his removal from American political life.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'I wasn’t sure … ': Mark Zuckerberg's hot mic moment with Donald Trump goes viral – watch
item.description: A White House dinner hosted by Donald Trump for tech leaders turned awkward when a hot mic caught Mark Zuckerberg admitting he inflated Meta's investment pledge. Other executives, including Tim Cook and Satya Nadella, also quantified their commitments, while Elon Musk was notably absent. The event highlighted Trump's evolving relationship with Silicon Valley despite earlier criticisms.

item.title: US tariffs: Trump signs order granting exemptions; zero duties begin Monday for aligned partners
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order granting tariff exemptions to trading partners who reach agreements on industrial exports, including metals, pharmaceuticals, and chemicals. This move aims to reshape global trade, reduce deficits, and encourage concessions from partner nations. The exemptions, effective Monday, cover goods not sufficiently produced in the U.S. and align with existing agreements, potentially impacting countries like Switzerland.
item.dc:creator: TOI Business Desk

item.title: Immigration raid: 100s of South Koreans held in US; Seoul vows 'all-out support'
item.description: Federal immigration agents raided a Hyundai plant in Georgia, detaining nearly 500 people, mostly South Korean nationals. This action has sparked outrage from Seoul, especially after President Lee's recent investment pledge to the US. The raid, involving multiple agencies, targeted alleged unlawful hiring practices.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Coldplay kiss-cam fallout: Former Astronomer HR Kristin Cabot files for divorce
item.description: Kristin Cabot, formerly of Astronomer, is divorcing Andrew Cabot, the CEO of Privateer Rum after her video with CEO Andy Byron went viral at a Coldplay concert. Andrew's ex-wife, Julia Cabot, says Andrew was unbothered by the incident as their marriage was already strained. Julia said Andrew Cabot is not a nice person and he had it coming as Boston Brahmins rarely put anyone above their ego.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: United Kingdom: Diwali celebrations in Leicester virtually cancelled; Hindu MP Shivani Raja speaks out
item.description: Leicester East MP Shivani Raja, one of the UK’s few Hindu MPs, has also raised the alarm. In a post on X, she wrote:“Our Diwali celebrations are STILL at risk. Diwali in Leicester is one of the biggest celebrations outside India – and the highlight of our city’s calendar. Yet Leicester City Council now want to limit celebrations, citing safety concerns. That’s why I, alongside Neil O’Brien MP, have written to the Chief Constable to press for solutions. We have to keep our Diwali celebrations safe.”
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

'Second in two days': Israel hits another Gaza high rise; witnesses watch 15-storey tower turn to dust - Video
item.description: Israeli forces struck the Sussi Tower in Gaza City, the second high-rise targeted in as many days, claiming Hamas used it for intelligence gathering. The military stated that precautions were taken to minimize civilian harm before the strike. This escalation occurs amid intensified Israeli operations and warnings for Gaza City residents to evacuate south.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Shabana Mahmood's anti-India statements go viral as Pak-origin Labor MP becomes UK Home Secretary
item.description: Shabana Mahmood, a Pakistani-origin Labour MP, has become the Home Secretary in a recent reshuffle, sparking controversy due to her past remarks on Kashmir. Her appointment comes as the government grapples with challenges related to Channel crossings and asylum issues. "England has fallen. My advice to non-Muslims is to get out now before it's too late," one wrote reacting to the Home Office's announcement.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Indian student Abhigyan Patel drowned at Bean Point Beach in Florida, area now marked as 'no-swim' zone
item.description: Abhigyan Patel, a 20-year-old Indian student, tragically drowned at Bean Point Beach on Anna Maria Island in Florida. Patel, part of a group of aviation students, was swept away while swimming, prompting a large-scale search. Following this and other recent incidents, the area has been designated a 'no-swim zone' due to dangerous currents.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Is Trump considering blocking IT outsourcing India? Aide says, 'Make call centers American again!'
item.description: Amid trade tensions as MAGA is increasing the pressure on the administration to stop programs that generate jobs in India, right-wing commentator Laura Loomer claimed Trump is considering blocking IT outsourcing to India. "Make Call Centers American Again!" Loomer posted on X. Loomer is not in administration or a policymaker but has gained prominence as Trump whisperer.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Opportunity for wisdom’: Hezbollah approves of Lebanon’s plan of monopoly over weapons; Israeli offensive still looms
item.description: Lebanon's cabinet endorsed an army plan to disarm Hezbollah, a move seen by some as a path to stability, while Hezbollah views it with suspicion. The US-brokered ceasefire's violation by Israel, as claimed by Lebanon, further complicates the situation. Disarmament efforts must address the economic needs of Hezbollah fighters and their families, highlighting the complexities of achieving lasting peace.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dubai traffic alert: Road to Centrepoint station closed as metro blue line work begins
item.description: Dubai has launched major transport upgrades, including the 30km Metro Blue Line and two new marine stations on Dubai Creek. The Blue Line, set to open in 2029, will ease congestion, link key districts, and cut airport travel to 20 minutes. The marine stations enhance water mobility, supporting Dubai’s vision for a smart, connected, and sustainable transport network.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Deep negotiations with Hamas’: Donald Trump urges release of Israeli hostages; warns of ‘nasty’ situation if not freed
item.description: Donald Trump stated that the US is engaged in “very deep” negotiations with Hamas, urging the group to immediately release all hostages held in Gaza. He cautioned that failure to do so would result in a “tough and nasty” situation. Trump's administration opposes partial hostage agreements and insists on the complete dismantling of Hamas before any release.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
